title: Playing private uptown parties and hauling a piano
summary: He played parties for wealthy families, including one needing a piano that Sylvester hauled by truck.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I said, the stream of the coast. How about? I said, the stream of the coast died the way it did back in the 30s. Because it was sure hitting for great things. Yeah.
But, I mean, just like I played for those people uptown. And, uh, several of them call me right now.

We sure miss out of good times. Old man, Carl, that had his, uh, Royalty place out here. He lived at number 19, uh, or something out here, right off of the Main Street. Right off of Carrollton Avenue, in other words. And, uh... Audubon Street. Audubon Place. That's right here. No, not our town. Yeah. That's back here, right up in Carrollton. You take Alleen Street, or Rename Street, and you go back. Take Alleen Street, and the first street you get after you cross Carrollton Avenue. They got a little street that runs in. I can't call the name of the street, but his house was around 19. And he would call me. I played for him this New Year's Eve. And about the 18th or the 20th of January. He said, Julius, don't forget next year. He'd hire me late then. You need the money? I said, no, I don't need anything. Now, this piano here, I bought that piano for $35. And a friend of mine, they had some old maids just on up there. If I'd open it, it's new. And, uh, so he told it to me for $35. Oh, I can't call the name of the place up here. They had a party in the yard. We grew up for Red Street, and, uh, on this side of the street, I can't even tell you, you play tennis and all like that up there. And they had a big party there one night. Now, they called me, Julius, we can't get a piano. Julius, we pay a hundred dollars for a piano. I said, you have to tell you where to go. You got piano. You gave me $35 for my piano. And I said, I think I can get it hauled for $25. Julius, we'll pay you. Sylvester have a little truck that's in his yard now. I called Sylvester and told him about it. And he brought his truck. The back of his truck is just about as long as the piano. And, uh, Albert Walter, he was supposed to play with me that night, but he couldn't play. So his son played with me. Albert Walter's son, he played trumpet with me. Piggy. So Piggy, he played with me that night, but I had Piggy and this one and that one, they all met him. And when Sylvester came, he backed his truck up to the door. When he backed up to the door, the piano and the truck, the door was just... All he had to do was roll it in there.
